mechanism_narrative: A higher level of housing starts (HOUST) indicates robust consumer demand and economic expansion, driving positive equity valuations and S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The Rank IC between HOUST and 20-day SPX returns is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate below 0.25% signals an ultra-accommodative monetary policy, compressing discount rates and boosting equity valuations, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are not significantly positive when FEDFUNDS < 0.25% (t-test p>0.05) or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS < 0.25%) combined with rising inflation (CPIAUCSL > 215) signals impending monetary tightening, depressing equity valuations and causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The interaction condition (FEDFUNDS < 0.25% AND CPIAUCSL > 215) occurs, but 60-day SPX returns are not significantly negative (t-test p>0.05) or the Rank IC for the interaction is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) exceeds 8%, it indicates a severe labor market contraction, which typically precedes economic recession and causes negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: UNRATE > 8% occurs, but 5-day SPX returns are not significantly negative (t-test p>0.05) or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A level of industrial production (INDPRO) below 100 (relative to 2017 baseline) indicates a below-trend economy, which leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: INDPRO < 100 occurs, but 5-day SPX returns are not significantly negative (t-test p>0.05) or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A higher level of employment (PAYEMS) indicates a strong labor market, which supports consumer spending and corporate earnings, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The Rank IC between PAYEMS and 60-day SPX returns is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is low and unemployment (UNRATE) is high, it indicates a 'jobless recovery' scenario, which leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The interaction condition (FEDFUNDS < 0.25% AND UNRATE > 8%) occurs, but 60-day SPX returns are not significantly negative (t-test p>0.05) or the Rank IC for the interaction is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) exceeds 215, it signals accelerating inflation, which triggers monetary policy tightening and causes negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: CPIAUCSL > 215 occurs, but 5-day SPX returns are not significantly negative (t-test p>0.05) or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.
